title: Google makes it easy to deepfake yourself
summary: YouTube Shorts is launching an AI feature that allows creators to make realistic digital avatars of themselves by recording a "live selfie" with specific prompts, which can then be used to generate new videos up to eight seconds long. The avatars come with restrictions including use only in creators' own videos, automatic watermarking as AI-generated content, and deletion after three years of inactivity. The rollout will be gradual and limited to creators 18 and older, coming as competitor OpenAI recently shut down its Sora video generation tool due to costs and controversies.

title: AI company's breached biometrics, ID document images make deepfake fraud easier
summary: Mercor, a $10 billion AI company that supplies training data to major firms like Anthropic, OpenAI and Meta, suffered a major data breach exposing ID documents and user biometric data including faces and voices. The breach was part of a wider supply chain attack on the open-source library LiteLLM, linked to hacking groups TeamPCP and Lapsus$, who claim to have stolen up to four terabytes of data. Security experts warn the stolen biometric data could enable widespread deepfake creation and fraud, while the incident highlights vulnerabilities in open-source components used across the AI industry.

title: Both radiologists and AI struggle to identify 'deepfake' X-rays
summary: A study published in Radiology found that both radiologists and AI struggle to distinguish deepfake radiographic images from authentic ones, raising concerns about potential fraud and cybersecurity risks in medical settings. Researchers tested 17 radiologists from multiple countries using AI-generated X-rays mixed with real patient images, and found the synthetic images were realistic enough to deceive even highly trained specialists. Experts warn this vulnerability could enable fraudulent litigation with fabricated injuries or allow hackers to manipulate patient diagnoses by injecting fake images into hospital systems.

title: Deepfake X-Rays Fool Radiologists and AI
summary: A study published in Radiology found that neither radiologists nor multimodal AI language models can reliably distinguish AI-generated "deepfake" X-ray images from authentic ones, with detection accuracy ranging from 58-92% for radiologists and 52-89% for AI models even when they knew synthetic images were present. The research, which involved 17 radiologists from six countries examining 264 X-rays (half real, half AI-generated), highlights significant vulnerabilities for healthcare systems, including risks of fraudulent litigation and cybersecurity threats if fake medical images are used to manipulate diagnoses. The findings underscore the urgent need for specialized tools and training to help medical professionals detect deepfakes and protect the integrity of digital medical records.

title: Deepfake Impersonation Attacks (Part 1): Anatomy of Modern Deepfakes
summary: In 2024, Arup's Hong Kong office lost $25.6 million when an employee was deceived by a video conference call featuring AI-generated deepfakes of multiple senior executives, including the CFO, who convinced the employee to execute 15 fraudulent transfers. The attack demonstrates how advances in generative AI, particularly diffusion models and voice cloning technology, now enable real-time impersonation attacks that bypass traditional security measures and liveness detection systems. Industry experts estimate deepfake-enabled fraud losses could reach $40 billion annually by 2027, requiring organizations to shift from perception-based identity verification to cryptographically verifiable mutual authentication systems.

title: Show HN: Air-gapped device to stop deepfake wire fraud
summary: A founder has built an air-gapped hardware device to prevent deepfake fraud in wire transfers, using a credit-card-sized device with no connectivity that displays transaction details and requires physical confirmation with cryptographic signing. The solution addresses a real threat demonstrated by Arup's $25.6M loss to deepfake fraud in 2024, where AI can now clone voices and faces convincingly enough to fool traditional verification methods like phone callbacks. title: Deepfake fraud taking place on an industrial scale, study finds
summary: Deepfake fraud has become widespread and "industrial" as AI tools for creating personalized scams are now cheap and accessible to anyone, according to AI experts. Researchers warn the technology is rapidly improving and becoming faster than expected, threatening to erode trust in digital communications and institutions.
